title: Treasury long-end buyback size increase takes effect ($4B/op, 10-30Y)
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0607 (dated August 19, 2026) states verbatim that the current maximum size of $2 billion per operation 'will be at least $4 billion per operation', for 'the 10-year to 20-year sector and the 20-year to 30-year sector', and that the change 'is effective September 9, 2026 and will be in effect for the remainder of this refunding quarter (through November 4, 2026)' — fetched direct via plain curl (HTTP 200) 2026-09-02. Promoted from estimate on that primary: WebFetch times out on home.treasury.gov but curl returns 200, the same tool artifact already recorded on treasury-borrowing-estimates-2026-11-02, checked 2026-09-02
notes: Bessent's 2026-08-19 announcement doubles nominal long-end liquidity-support buyback operations (10-20Y and 20-30Y sectors) from a $2B to a $4B/operation minimum, effective this date through the refunding quarter's close (2026-11-04) — a fiscal-liquidity support for long-end demand technicals landing the day before the 30Y reopening (09-10). Discovered during the treasury-30y-bond-2026-09-10 pulse-check adjacency sweep; not previously a dated calendar entry. Promoted estimate -> confirmed on the directly-fetched primary during this event's own 2026-09-02 pulse check, which is exactly the kill switch its ledger registered ('the treasury.gov primary becoming directly fetchable'). CONFIRMED HERE MEANS THE DATE AND SIZES, NOT AN EFFECT: the release's own next sentence, 'An updated tentative Treasury buyback schedule will be released at a later date', is still unfulfilled 16 days on (re-checked at the primary 2026-09-04: the posted PDF's masthead still reads 'For Publication August 5, 2026' and both long-end rows still cap at $2B), which is why treasury-buyback-10y20y-2026-09-10 (est) still carries the superseded $2B cap. AND THIS DATE IS AN ELIGIBILITY DATE, NOT AN OPERATION: the schedule lists no long-end buyback on 09-09 itself — that day's only operation is a $12.5B cash-management buyback in the 1Mo-2Y sector (announced 09-08) — so the first test of the $4B floor is the 10-20Y operation on 09-10, and the 09-09 operation announcement (preliminary CUSIP list 11:00am ET) is the first place a hard number can appear. The program's only market test to date faded inside a day (10Y -6bp on 08-19, fully round-tripped +5bp by 08-20, and ~4.77% by 09-01 — above where it sat pre-announcement). No house playbook is rates-keyed; this stays context for the Sep 1 -> Sep 16 corridor. AMENDED 2026-09-08 by this event's own D-1 pulse check; status, date, sizes and impact UNCHANGED, two mechanics added from Treasury's own operations data (fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations, plain curl HTTP 200, read directly for the first time rather than through press narration). (1) THE $2B CAP WAS BINDING, NOT DEMAND: since 2024-05 the 10Y-20Y bucket accepted the full cap in 25 of 25 operations and 20Y-30Y in 24 of 26, on offers never below $6.4B (10Y-20Y median $19.7B, max $36.0B); the two exceptions are 20Y-30Y accepting $205M against $36.0B offered on 2026-03-19 and $785M against $25.4B on 2025-11-20, which is the standing proof Treasury can ration on price as well as size. So doubling the cap should convert into executed par, not just headroom. (2) BUT IT IS PARITY, NOT ESCALATION: every other nominal sector on the same schedule already ran a $4B cap before sb0607 existed - 1Mo-2Y (08/06), 3Y-5Y (08/21), 5Y-7Y (08/26), 7Y-10Y (09/17), 2Y-3Y (10/06) - and only 10Y-20Y and 20Y-30Y sat at $2B, so this removes the long end's discount rather than creating a new tier. Scale stays small either way: +$2B per operation across the seven long-end ops in the 09-09 to 11-04 window is roughly +$14B over eight weeks, against $61B of 10Y ($39B, 09-09) plus 30Y ($22B, 09-10) issuance in this single week - reopening sizes IDENTICAL to June's, which mechanically corroborates Bessent's stated 'auctions will continue as usual despite the expanded buyback program.' The programme adds to demand and subtracts nothing from supply. Neither finding is directional and the stance is unchanged. The promised updated tentative schedule remains unpublished at 20 days (re-fetched 2026-09-08, HTTP 200, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35, byte-identical to the 09-03/09-05/09-06 fetches). CLOSED OUT 2026-09-10 (see docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09.md -> ## Outcome); status, date and impact UNCHANGED, but two mechanics above are now superseded by the primary and are corrected here. (A) THE PROMISED UPDATED SCHEDULE PUBLISHED ON THE EVENT'S OWN DATE: masthead 'For Publication September 9, 2026', 89,250 bytes, md5 c49a5351bf2d31a367817abc62be51bd, against the stale edition's 125,547 bytes / md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35. It does NOT set a $4B cap - every 10Y-20Y and 20Y-30Y row from 09-24 through 11-04 reads '= or > $4 billion', a FLOOR WITH DISCRETION, where every other sector keeps a hard number ($4 billion for 7Y-10Y 09-17, 2Y-3Y 10-06 and 1Mo-2Y 11-05; $500 million TIPS 09-15; $750 million TIPS 09-29 and 10-21). The one long-end row carrying a number, 09-10 10Y-20Y, was set at $6 BILLION - 3x the old cap, not 2x - which is inside sb0607's 'at least $4 billion' language and therefore NOT an expansion of announced policy. (B) THE FIRST ENLARGED OPERATION EXECUTED 09-10: fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations reports $10,489,000,000 offered and $5,187,000,000 accepted across 23 of 40 eligible issues - the first 10Y-20Y operation since 2024-05 NOT to fill its ceiling (25/25 becomes 25/26), so the binding constraint moved from $2B to roughly $5.2B rather than to $6B. The window's incremental buying is therefore nearer +$21B than the +$14B estimated on 09-08. NONE OF THIS WAS DIRECTIONAL: on the same afternoon the 30Y (5.37%) and 20Y (5.39%) posted their highest par closes of 2026 across all 174 sessions in the year's CSV, firing the ledger's 'fresh cycle high despite the larger operations running' kill switch. The mover was inflation, not the buyback - August PPI final demand printed +0.40% m/m SA and +5.44% y/y NSA (BLS API) against a +0.3% consensus, and the curve bear-flattened (2Y +13bp, 30Y +9bp), so the sector Treasury was buying outperformed. Coupon sizes unchanged a second time: the 09-10 coupon announcement's 20Y reopening is $13B on 09-15, identical to 06-16's. The stand-aside stance closed intact.
